title: Response-Level Claim to Evidence Verification (Phase 4)
context: Phase 3 typed tool results, but nothing verified the generated reply against what the runtime established this turn; a model could claim success after a FAILED tool result or assert stale memory as current state. The AURA 2.0 contract Phase 4 requires a deterministic, no-second-model verification boundary over free-form chat that does not make ordinary knowledge conversation unusable.
decision: brain/verify adds ClaimState (VERIFIED/SUPPORTED/INFERRED/UNKNOWN/CONTRADICTED), VerifierDecision (PASS/REPAIR/MARK_UNCERTAIN/ASK_CLARIFICATION/REFUSE_UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM), deterministic claim extraction scoped by a closed world-object vocabulary, a request-scoped EvidenceLedger reusing the canonical Phase 3 Evidence, rules that make SUCCESS+postcondition the only path to a verified action claim while FAILED/DENIED/UNAVAILABLE/UNKNOWN contradict or leave ungrounded success language, and minimal per-sentence repair that only moves claims downward in certainty. ConversationManager builds the ledger per turn, captures tool and memory evidence, and verifies the final text on both chat and chat_stream (repaired text in StreamFinishedEvent; fragments stream raw and this is documented, not hidden). The launcher injects the verifier from response.verify config; enabled:false restores the pre-Phase-4 pipeline.
alternatives: A second model call to judge the reply
Buffering the entire stream before delivery
Verifying every sentence including general knowledge
rejected_alternatives: A second model call (non-deterministic, slow, moves the boundary instead of closing it)
Full stream buffering (retracts latency for a path that runs no tools; finished-event replacement chosen instead)
Grounding ordinary knowledge (hedging general facts makes normal chat unusable)
consequences: Action success claims require verified evidence; confident phrasing adds no certainty; memory is attributed rather than asserted and conflicts surface instead of resolving silently; capability claims are checked against the live registry; diagnostics stay metadata-only. Limitations are explicit: deterministic extraction is incomplete by design, streamed fragments reach the UI before verification, and this reduces overclaiming without eliminating hallucinations.
